instructions: Local-first decentralized social app (Next.js 16, React 19 with the React Compiler, Dexie/IndexedDB, Zustand, TanStack Query, Tailwind v4, Shadcn UI). AGENTS.md (attached for every file via files.json) is the agent entry point and lists the hard constraints and non-negotiables; docs/ is canonical and the per-path docs are attached via files.json. Architecture enforcement is critical: check layer boundary violations (controllers -> application -> services -> models), the ADR-0009 cross-application allow-list, local-first read/write rules and TTL updates. Imports go through the tsconfig path aliases to concrete modules (no index.ts barrels, no src/config/index.ts, @/config/<module>, @/app/routes). Apply the code-quality rules in docs/development-workflow.md (suppressed lints need a reason, no dead code, no unused exports, no manual memoization, scrutinize optional parameters). Verify every finding in source before commenting.

rules.rule: Controllers must NOT import from services directly. All IO must go through the Application layer.
Coordinators must NOT call Application directly. They must go through Controllers.
Application layer must NOT access Zustand stores directly. Stores are managed by Controllers.
Pipes must be pure functions. No IO, no database access, no network calls.
Do not log errors before throwing Err.* factories. Err.* factories log automatically. Logging then throwing causes double-logged errors.

Only PostApplication, NotificationApplication, BootstrapApplication, MigrationApplication, HotApplication, PostStreamApplication, and TtlApplication may call other Applications. Max call depth is 1 by default. The only permitted depth-2 paths are PostApplication, NotificationApplication, or TtlApplication calling PostStreamApplication, which may call FileApplication for attachment persistence. All other depth-2 paths, paths of depth 3 or greater, and cycles are forbidden.
Always check for Shadcn equivalent components before creating custom UI. Use Shadcn primitives as base.

Stock Lucide icons: import from 'lucide-react' only. Custom/brand SVG components: import from '@/icons' (tsconfig alias → src/libs/icons/icons.tsx). Do not re-export lucide-react from @/libs or add export * from 'lucide-react' through aggregate index files. URL→icon helpers (getIconFromUrl, getLabelFromUrl) belong in @/libs/utils (urlToIcon). See docs/components.md — Icons.
Never hardcode counts or quantities in skeleton components. Source from constants or props.

Avoid index.ts / index.tsx files that only re-export from children, and avoid pushing symbols through intermediate re-export modules without a strong reason. That pattern adds indirection, confuses go-to-definition, makes circular deps harder to trace, and can defeat tree-shaking. Import from the defining source file. Hooks and core layers: use @/hooks/*, @/controllers/*, @/services/*, @/models/*, @/stores/*. Config: @/config/<module> only (no src/config/index.ts aggregate). Routes: @/app/routes. Components: no src/components/**/index.ts or index.tsx that only re-export; import concrete files via @/atoms/*, @/molecules/*, @/organisms/*, @/templates/* (for example @/atoms/Button/Button).

Every eslint-disable, eslint-disable-next-line, @ts-ignore, and @ts-expect-error must have an adjacent comment explaining WHY the suppression is needed. Bare suppressions hide real bugs. If a rule is wrong for the whole file, use a top-level eslint-disable with rationale rather than sprinkling inline ignores.

Remove unreachable branches, unused variables, commented-out blocks, and code guarded by conditions that are always true or false. Dead code misleads readers and inflates bundle size. Don't comment code out 'for later' — git preserves history. If a feature flag is permanently on/off, collapse the branch.

If a function, const, type, or class is exported but never imported by any other file, remove the export or demote to a local. Stale exports clutter the public API surface. Only exception: symbols consumed by external packages or test harnesses — add a comment like '// exported for integration tests'.

When a function has 3+ optional parameters that change its behavior (not just defaults), it likely hides multiple responsibilities. Prefer an options object, explicit overloads, or separate functions. A single function with many optional params makes call sites ambiguous and testing harder.

This project uses the React Compiler which auto-memoizes renders and callbacks. Manual useCallback and useMemo are redundant in most cases and add visual noise. Flag them unless the author cites a specific reason the compiler can't handle it (e.g., ref-stable callback for a non-React subscriber, or profiler evidence of a hotspot).

Controller method names encode IO: fetch* (network only), get* (local only), getMany* (bulk local, returns Map<Pubky, T>), getOrFetch* and getMany*OrFetch (local first, network fallback), subscribe* (long-lived stream subscription), commitCreate*/commitUpdate*/commitDelete* (local-first write + sync). Flag load*/save*/retrieve*/create*/remove* style names. See docs/local-first.md.

Local-first reads in hooks must use useLocalFirstQuery (@/hooks/useLocalFirstQuery/useLocalFirstQuery): queryFn is a pure get* controller read run inside useLiveQuery, fetchFn is a fetch* controller that persists to Dexie. Flag network calls, TanStack Query or retry logic inside a useLiveQuery callback (breaks Dexie PSD, ADR-0011), new hand-rolled useEffect + useLiveQuery pairs, and read paths that do not handle a settled null (missing) or a soft-deleted tombstone. See docs/local-first.md.

Every local write must refresh the affected entity's *_ttl row (lastUpdatedAt) and persist dependencies before dependents (author, then post, then tags). Flag writes that skip the TTL update (the cache then never refreshes) and stream invalidation that deletes stream rows eagerly instead of marking the scope dirty in postStreamDirtyRegistry. See docs/data-patterns.md and docs/local-first.md.

There is one Dexie schema version (4 since the social v1 port) and no migration chain: a DB_VERSION mismatch deletes and recreates the local database (ADR-0019, docs/data-patterns.md). Any change to DB_VERSION, a table's index map or the stores() definition must be called out in the PR as a deliberate data-loss decision, and a DB_VERSION change also needs the CI-task PR for the Docker build arg; flag it when it arrives as a side effect of a feature.

Re-throw AppError unchanged and normalize unknowns with toAppError(); use safeFetch + httpResponseToError (or the service's *.utils.ts wrapper) for HTTP instead of raw fetch. Narrow availability exceptions: ClientRegionService.fetchCountry uses raw fetch for the optional Shop region probe, returning unavailable for every failure without throwing, logging or reporting; LocksService.isServerReady similarly returns a boolean. Do not extend these exceptions to ordinary data reads or writes. Branch on error.category / error.code, never on message strings, except the documented pinned Pubky SDK 0.16 checks in HomeserverService/GrantFlowService and Locks SDK 0.1.0 isLockServerRegionBlocked: only a non-AppError Error named InvalidInput with exact message 'Lock Server viewer request failed with HTTP 451' becomes a regionBlocked result before Err.* construction. SDK contract and regression tests are required. No raw `throw new Error()` in src/core production code, except sdkError in the Cypress-only locks.e2eStub.ts, which mirrors the SDK's own error shape on purpose. See docs/error-handling.md.

Errors reach Sentry and, in a consenting browser, Pulse through Err.* factories. Flag direct Sentry.captureException or Pulse.captureException calls anywhere except the captureAppError funnel in src/libs/observability/sentry.ts, the single Pulse capture in src/libs/error/error.factories.ts, and the two error boundaries src/app/error.tsx and src/app/global-error.tsx (which capture only non-AppError instances); flag Sentry.setUser or Pulse.setUser with PII; flag Pulse tracking added outside the consent gate in src/libs/observability/pulse.ts, and raw pathnames added to the pulseScreenName allowlist; flag Err.* context that carries raw user data not covered by the scrubber in src/libs/observability/sentry.utils.ts (the key list lives in docs/sentry.md, Privacy).

Toast title and description must be static product copy. Flag any user-entered value (feed or tag names, display names, file names, free text) interpolated into toast() copy; bounded values such as config constants, small counts and authored Err.* messages are fine. See docs/components.md, Toasts.

Forms use react-hook-form + zod (@hookform/resolvers/zod) behind a use{Action}Form hook that returns { form, submit, reset }; the schema, *_FORM_FIELDS map, types and defaults live in a sibling *.types.ts; fields render Controller via ControlledInputField / ControlledTextareaField; validation messages are literal US-English strings; use z.url() not z.string().url(). Flag form components that call commit* controllers directly instead of going through a use{Action}Form hook, and hand-rolled form state. See docs/components.md, Forms.

Use semantic design tokens (bg-primary, text-muted-foreground) and the Tailwind scale. Flag hardcoded hex/rgb colours (bg-[#1a1a1a]), fixed-length arbitrary values (p-[13px], h-[37px]) and z-index values outside -z-10, z-10, z-30, z-40, z-50, z-60. Do not flag arbitrary values the scale cannot express: a viewport fraction with no named utility (max-h-[75dvh]; the full viewport is h-dvh, max-h-screen, max-w-screen, so flag h-[100dvh] or max-w-[100vw]), calc() over the viewport or a CSS variable (max-h-[calc(100dvh-2rem)] in the Dialog atom) and CSS variables set by a library (var(--radix-…)). See docs/components.md and docs/z-index.md.

i18n was removed (#2313): user-facing copy is an inline US-English literal at the call site. Flag any next-intl import, useTranslations / useFormatter / t.rich usage, a messages/ directory, src/i18n, or a lookalike message registry or translation map. See docs/migrations/2305-i18n-conflict-guide.md.

A visual change to a surface covered by a VRT (src/test/vrt/<area>/*.vrt.test.tsx) needs its baseline regenerated by the VRT Update Baselines workflow; PR CI does not run VRT and locally generated baselines must not be committed. If the PR changes such a surface without mentioning the baseline impact, ask the author to state it. See docs/visual-regression-testing.md.
These files are generated (lucideIcons.ts itself is hand-written). Flag any hand edit and ask for the generator to be re-run instead.

The service worker owns the app shell only: precache, the share target and the static offline fallback. Do not add runtime caching for homeserver, pkarr, httprelay, Nexus, CDN or any data (Dexie is the only data cache; TTL is the only freshness mechanism), no defaultCache, and keep skipWaiting false (updates are user-consented via useServiceWorkerUpdate). One recorded exception: the social v1 cut-over ships skipWaiting true plus an activate listener that claims and navigates every window (ADR-0021 amendment) until PR-E2 reverts it on the team's decision; flag any other takeover, and flag a change to the pubky-social-migrator precache exclude (the migrator must stay a dynamic import). Public precache entries are an allow-list in globPublicPatterns. See docs/pwa.md and ADR-0021.

Every homeserver PUT and DELETE goes through HomeserverService (request, putBlob, delete), which retries 429, 500, 503 and the GCS publish-conflict 409 in retryHomeserverWrite. Flag any direct SDK storage write or raw homeserver fetch outside it, and any new retry of another 409, 412 or 423. A write whose body comes from a homeserver read of the same data must pass the fence from HomeserverService.createWriteFence() and wrap the read and the write in retryHomeserverWriteAfterReread(fence, ...): the fenced write makes one attempt, every retried status (429, 500, 503, the publish conflict) runs the read again, and no later pass runs after logout; flag one that replays a read-dependent body or omits the fence (a post edit re-reads the head version, a profile, feed or settings edit re-reads the stored object). The social v1 migrator behind HomeserverService.migrateToSocialV1 owns its transport retries outside retryHomeserverWrite (ADR-0026); HomeserverService.deleteIdempotent and ProfileApplication.deleteFile are attempt loops over single-attempt HomeserverService.delete calls, not a policy of their own; flag any other retry of a homeserver write. Notifications' last_read must never move backward. See docs/error-handling.md.

Homeserver objects are built, decoded and encoded by pubky-social-specs (buildPost, editPost, buildTag, buildFollow, buildMute, buildBookmark, buildFeed, buildUser, buildFile, buildUri, decodeObject, encodeObject, deletionPaths, listPrefix) and written as the built bytes with HomeserverService.putBlob(built.body) or removed with deleteIdempotent over deletionPaths. Flag a homeserver path spelled by hand (/pub/social/v1/..., /priv/social/v1/..., /pub/pubky.app/...; only src/config/app-files.ts names the app's own /priv/app.pubky/v1/ files, and src/config/auth.ts its capability scope), a JSON.stringify or hand-built body for a data-model object, any import of pubky-social-specs/client outside src/test-utils, a write of the 0.x spelling (/pub/pubky.app/ is read as a fallback and never written; its copies are removed per object through deletionPaths where the data model names them, and in full by the account deletion, which lists the legacy tree), a post edit that overwrites a version instead of writing the next one, an edit that rebuilds an object from a local row instead of spreading the decoded stored object ($unknown must survive), a short/long written to the homeserver (the local vocabulary crosses to note/article only in toLocalPostKind/toStoredPostKind), and media deleted on an edit or avatar change (content-addressed files are shared; only a post delete collects, after the reference checks). See docs/data-patterns.md, docs/local-first.md, ADR-0027 and docs/migrations/social-v1.md.

A post has two spellings while the 0.x tree exists (pubky://{owner}/pub/social/v1/posts/{id} and pubky://{owner}/pub/pubky.app/posts/{id}) and Nexus may serve either. Flag any comparison of a post URI against one spelling: reduce it to a composite id (buildCompositeIdFromPubkyUri is form-agnostic, version paths included) or match both through postReferenceSpellings (src/core/pipes/post/post.reference.ts). New references are written in the v1 spelling. The 0.x spellings that stay in src/** are the PERMANENT allow-list of src/core/services/homeserver/social-v1-compliance.gate.test.ts, each with a reason: a new 0.x match is ported, never added there. See docs/local-first.md and docs/migrations/social-v1.md.

Bookmarks (/priv/social/v1/bookmarks/), mutes (/priv/social/v1/mutes/) and feeds (/priv/social/v1/feeds/) are private objects Nexus never sees, and the local tables are their source of truth, hydrated by a LIST at bootstrap and in the DB-reset resync (ADR-0028, ADR-0014). Flag any read of a Nexus bookmark field (post.bookmark, counts.bookmarks, source=bookmarks), any code that treats these objects or the app files under /priv/app.pubky/v1/ (settings.json, last_read.json) as public or indexed, any stream cursor or Nexus page for the bookmarks stream (it is cache only), and any session-bound homeserver event stream (eventStreamForUser(...).session(...)) or /priv/ path registered on the shared stream: private files are polled (MuteListSyncCoordinator, NotificationLastReadPollCoordinator), because a session-bound stream's lease is unbounded while its response headers are outstanding (pubky/pubky-homeserver#798, ADR-0014, ADR-0029).

Every restore and sign-in passes the social v1 migration gate before the session enters the auth store (restoreStatus 'social-migration', AuthStatus.NEEDS_SOCIAL_MIGRATION, route /migration; ADR-0026). Flag a new route that is reachable while that status holds (RouteGuardProvider redirects everything but /migration, /logout and the legal pages to /migration; a new guard set must keep that), a coordinator started outside CoordinatorsManager's gate or keyed on the session alone, a provider or hook that treats the status as 'ready' or opens sign-in over it, any code that hand-writes the _migrated.json flag, and any epoch or 'is migrated' check in feature code (every signed-in account has passed the gate, so none is needed). Capability strings live only in src/config/auth.ts (APP_CAPABILITIES, SOCIAL_V1_APP_CAPABILITIES, LOCKS_CAPABILITIES).

Every Nexus URL is built by buildNexusUrl under NEXUS_API_VERSION (/v1); the one /v0 call is filesApi.getFiles (POST v0/files/by_ids, 0.x attachment metadata, asked once per fetched page before the posts persist). /v1 serves note/article, no bookmark fields, no file details and no tag relationship, so every response is folded once at the read boundary before anything is stored or compared: the kind fold (note/article to short/long, fail-open) in PostNormalizer.fromNexus, NotificationNormalizer.toLocalKind and the server-side fetchUserAndPostForMetadata, and the tag fold (relationship = relationship ?? tag_uri != null) in TagNormalizer.fromNexus, applied to the tags of a post or a user by PostNormalizer.fromNexus and UserNormalizer.fromNexus, and every kind= the app sends is the stored name (toNexusPostKindFilter). Flag a literal v0 path, a kind read from a Nexus response without the fold, a short/long in a Nexus URL, exclude_kinds, a second by_ids request per card where a per-page fetch exists, and a v1 address (files/{hash}.{ext}) sent to files/by_ids. See ADR-0027, Nexus API version.

Tests use the real pubky-social-specs and pubky-social-migrator: flag vi.mock('pubky-social-specs'), vi.mock('pubky-social-migrator') or a hand-rolled double of their builders. Keys come from fakeOwner (pubky-social-specs/testing), deterministic ids and created_at from setClock through freezeSpecClock / withFrozenSpecClock (src/test-utils/spec-clock.ts), and the homeserver from stubMemoryHomeserver (src/test-utils/homeserver.ts) rather than spies on putBlob arguments; post ids in fixtures are 13 Crockford characters and keys real z-base32. See docs/development-workflow.md, Verification.
